sentences.zh: 周室諸王

translations.literal: Zhou House various kings
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the Northern Zhou Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十六周室諸王

translations.literal: Biography forty-six Zhou House various kings
translations.idiomatic: Biography 46: Princes of the Northern Zhou Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 文帝十三王孝閔帝一王明帝二王武帝六王宣帝二王

translations.literal: Wen Emperor thirteen kings Xiao Min Emperor one king Ming Emperor two kings Wu Emperor six kings Xuan Emperor two kings
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen sons of Emperor Wen; one prince under Emperor Xiaomin; two under Emperor Ming; six under Emperor Wu; two under Emperor Xuan

sentences.zh: 周文帝十三子：姚夫人生明帝。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen Emperor thirteen sons: Lady Yao bore Ming Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen sons of Emperor Wen of Zhou: Lady Yao bore Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 後宮生宋獻公震。

translations.literal: Rear palace bore Song Duke Gong Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: A lady of the rear palace bore Duke Gong Zhen of Song, Zhen.

sentences.zh: 文元皇后生孝閔皇帝。

translations.literal: Wen Yuan Empress bore Xiao Min Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuanwen bore Emperor Xiaomin.

sentences.zh: 文宣叱奴皇后生武帝、衛剌王直。

translations.literal: Wen Xuan Chinu Empress bore Wu Emperor, Wei Thorn King Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chinu bore Emperor Wu and Prince Zhi of Wei.

sentences.zh: 達步妃生齊煬王憲。

translations.literal: Dabu consort bore Qi Flaming King Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Dabu bore Prince Xian of Qi.

sentences.zh: 王姬生趙僭王招。

translations.literal: Wang Ji bore Zhao Overreaching King Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: A royal concubine bore Prince Zhao of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 後宮生譙孝王儉、陳惑王純、越野王盛、代紘王達、冀康公通、滕聞王逌。

translations.literal: Rear palace bore Qiao Xiao King Jian, Chen Huo King Chun, Yue Ye King Sheng, Dai Hong King Da, Ji Kang Duke Tong, Teng Wen King You.
translations.idiomatic: The rear palace bore Prince Xiao of Qiao, Jian; Prince Huo of Chen, Chun; Prince Yue of Yue, Sheng; Prince Hong of Dai, Da; Duke Kang of Ji, Tong; and Prince Wen of Teng, You.

sentences.zh: 無子，以明帝第三子實嗣。

translations.literal: No sons, took Ming Emperor third son Shi as heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; Emperor Ming's third son Shi was adopted as his heir.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Jiande third year, advanced rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande his rank was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 大象中，為大前疑，尋為隋文帝害，國除。

translations.literal: Daxiang within, made Grand Mentor, soon by Sui Wen Emperor harmed, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era he served as Grand Mentor, but was soon killed by Emperor Wen of Sui and his fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 衛剌王直，字豆羅突。

translations.literal: Wei Thorn King Zhi, style Douluotu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhi of Wei, style name Douluotu.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年，封秦郡公。

translations.literal: Wei Gong Emperor third year, enfeoffed Qin commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qin commandery.

sentences.zh: 武成初，進封衛國公，曆雍州牧、大司空、襄州總管。

translations.literal: Wucheng beginning, advanced enfeoff Wei state duke, passed through Yong province governor, Grand Minister of Works, Xiang province commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng he was advanced to Duke of Wei and successively served as governor of Yong province, Grand Minister of Works, and commissioner over Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 直，武帝母弟也，性浮詭。

translations.literal: Zhi, Wu Emperor uterine younger brother also, nature frivolous deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was the uterine younger brother of Emperor Wu; his nature was frivolous and deceitful.

sentences.zh: 以晉公護執政，遂貳於帝而昵護。

translations.literal: Because Jin Duke Hu held government, then turned from emperor yet intimate with Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Duke of Jin, Hu, held power, he turned against the emperor while remaining intimate with Hu.

sentences.zh: 及南討軍敗，慍於免黜，又請帝除護。

translations.literal: When southern campaign army defeated, resentful at dismissal, again asked emperor remove Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern campaign failed he grew resentful at being dismissed and again asked the emperor to remove Hu.

sentences.zh: 帝宿有誅護意，遂與直謀之。

translations.literal: Emperor long had execute Hu intent, then with Zhi plotted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long wished to execute Hu and therefore plotted with Zhi.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，帝以齊王憲為大塚宰。

translations.literal: When Hu executed, emperor made Qi King Xian Grand Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu was killed, the emperor made Prince Xian of Qi Grand Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 直既乖本望，又請為大司馬，欲擅威權。

translations.literal: Zhi already missed original hope, again asked to be Grand Minister of War, wished monopolize authority.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, having missed his original hopes, next asked to be made Grand Minister of War, seeking to monopolize authority.

sentences.zh: 帝知其意，謂曰：「汝兄弟長幼有序，何反居下列也？」

translations.literal: Emperor knew his intent, said: "You brothers senior junior have order, why instead dwell below rank?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew his intent and said, "Among you brothers there is an order of seniority — why would you insist on ranking below?"

sentences.zh: 以為大司徒。

translations.literal: Made Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Minister of Education instead.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Jiande third year, advanced rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande his rank was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以直第為東宮，更使直自擇所居。

translations.literal: At first, emperor took Zhi residence for Eastern Palace, again had Zhi himself choose dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor had taken Zhi's residence for the Eastern Palace and had Zhi choose another place to live.

sentences.zh: 直曆觀府署，無稱意者，至廢陟屺佛寺，遂欲居之。

translations.literal: Zhi passed through viewing government offices, none pleasing, arrived at abandoned Zhiqi Buddhist temple, then wished dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi went through all the government offices and found none to his liking; when he came to the abandoned Qiji Buddhist monastery at Mount Zhi, he wished to live there.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲謂曰：「弟兒女成長，此寺偏小，詎是所宜？」

translations.literal: Qi King Xian said: "Younger brother sons daughters grown, this temple rather small, how is it suitable?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi said to him, "Brother, your sons and daughters are grown — this temple is too small; how can it be suitable?"

sentences.zh: 直曰：「一身尚不自容，何論兒女！」

translations.literal: Zhi said: "One body still not self-contained, what discuss sons daughters!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "I cannot even find room for myself — what does it matter about sons and daughters!"

sentences.zh: 憲怪而疑之。

translations.literal: Xian wondered and suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was astonished and grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 直嘗從帝校獵而亂行，帝怒，對眾撻之。

translations.literal: Zhi once followed emperor military hunt yet marched out of line, emperor angry, before crowd flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhi followed the emperor on a hunting outing and marched out of line; the emperor was angry and flogged him in public.

sentences.zh: 自是，憤怨滋甚。

translations.literal: From this, hatred resentment ever more.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his hatred and resentment grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 及帝幸雲陽宮，直在京師反，攻肅章門，司武尉遲運閉門，不得入，退走。

translations.literal: When emperor visited Yunyang Palace, Zhi at capital rebelled, attacked Suozhang Gate, Martial Affairs Yuchi Yun closed gate, could not enter, retreated fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Yunyang Palace, Zhi rebelled in the capital, attacked the Suozhang Gate; Commandant of Martial Affairs Yuchi Yun closed the gate and would not admit him, so he retreated.

sentences.zh: 追至荊州獲之，免為庶人，囚諸宮中。

translations.literal: Pursued to Jing province captured him, removed as commoner, imprisoned within palace.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued to Jing province he was captured, degraded to commoner, and imprisoned within the palace.

sentences.zh: 尋有異志，及其子十人並誅之，國除。

translations.literal: Soon had other intent, and his ten sons together executed, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he harbored further designs; he and his ten sons were all executed and the fief abolished.

sentences.zh: 武成初，除益州總管，進封齊國公。

translations.literal: Wucheng beginning, removed as Yi province commissioner, advanced enfeoff Qi state duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng he was appointed commissioner over Yi province and advanced to Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 初，平蜀之後，文帝以其形勝之地，不欲使宿將居之。

translations.literal: At first, after pacifying Shu, Wen Emperor because its strategic terrain, did not wish old generals dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Shu, Emperor Wen, because it was a strategically critical region, did not wish an old general to reside there.

sentences.zh: 諸子中欲有推擇，偏問武帝以下，誰欲此行，並未及對，而憲先請。

translations.literal: Among sons wished to choose, separately asked Wu Emperor and below who wished this journey, all not yet answered, yet Xian first requested.
translations.idiomatic: Among his sons he wished to choose one; he asked Emperor Wu and those below who would go — before any had answered, Xian volunteered first.

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「刺史當撫眾臨人，非爾所及。

translations.literal: Wen Emperor said: "Regional inspector ought comfort masses oversee men, not your reach.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said, "A regional inspector must comfort the masses and oversee men — that is not your level.

sentences.zh: 以年授者，當歸爾兄。」

translations.literal: By age granted, ought return to your elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: By age it should go to your elder brother."

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「才用殊不關大小，試而無效，甘受面欺。」

translations.literal: Xian said: "Talent use especially not concern great small, trial yet no effect, willingly accept face deception."
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "Talent has nothing to do with great or small; if a trial fails I am willing to be shamed to my face."

sentences.zh: 文帝以憲年尚幼，未之遣。

translations.literal: Wen Emperor because Xian years still young, did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, because Xian was still young, did not send him.

sentences.zh: 明帝追遵先旨，故有此授。

translations.literal: Ming Emperor followed prior intent, therefore had this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming followed his father's prior intent, hence this appointment.

sentences.zh: 憲時年十六，善於撫綏，留心政術，辭訟輻湊，聽受不疲。

translations.literal: Xian then years sixteen, skilled at comforting pacifying, attentive to governance arts, lawsuits crowded, heard accepted not weary.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was then sixteen; skilled at comforting and pacifying, attentive to governance; lawsuits crowded in and he heard them without tiring.

sentences.zh: 蜀人悅之，共立碑頌德。

translations.literal: Shu people pleased with him, together set stele praise virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu were pleased and together set up a stele praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 保定中，徵拜雍州牧。

translations.literal: Baoding within, summoned appointed Yong province governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoding era he was summoned and appointed governor of Yong province.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護東伐，以尉遲迥為前鋒，圍洛陽。

translations.literal: When Jin Duke Hu attacked east, made Yuchi Jiong vanguard, besieged Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Jin, Hu, attacked eastward, Yuchi Jiong was made vanguard and besieged Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 齊兵數萬，奄出軍後，諸軍恇駭，並各退散。

translations.literal: Qi troops several tens of thousands, suddenly came out behind army, all armies terrified, each retreated scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of thousands of Qi troops suddenly came out behind the army; the armies were terrified and all scattered in retreat.

sentences.zh: 唯憲與王雄、達奚武拒之，而雄為齊人所敗，三軍震懼。

translations.literal: Only Xian with Wang Xiong, Daxi Wu resisted them, yet Xiong by Qi men defeated, three armies shaken fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xian with Wang Xiong and Daxi Wu resisted; Xiong was defeated by the Qi men and the whole army was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 憲親自督勵，眾心乃安。

translations.literal: Xian personally supervised urged, masses' hearts then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Xian personally urged them on and the men's hearts were then at ease.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護執政，雅相親委，賞罰之際，皆得預焉。

translations.literal: At that time Jin Duke Hu held government, elegantly mutually trusted, reward punishment occasions, all could participate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Duke of Jin, Hu, held power and treated him with great trust; in matters of reward and punishment he was always consulted.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，以憲為大司馬，行小塚宰，雍州牧如故。

translations.literal: Tianhe third year, made Xian Grand Minister of War, acting junior minister of war, Yong province governor as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he was made Grand Minister of War, acting as junior minister of war, while remaining governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 四年，齊將獨孤永業來寇，詔憲與柱國李穆出宜陽，築崇德等五城，絕其糧道。

translations.literal: Fourth year, Qi general Dugu Yongye came raid, ordered Xian with pillar Li Mu out Yiyang, built Chongde and five cities, cut their grain route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Qi general Dugu Yongye came to raid; the emperor ordered Xian with the pillar Li Mu to go out to Yiyang and build five walled cities including Chongde to cut their grain route.

sentences.zh: 齊將斛律明月築壘洛南。

translations.literal: Qi general Hulu Yueyang built ramparts Luo south.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi general Hulu Yueyang built fortifications south of Luo.

sentences.zh: 五年，憲涉洛邀之，明月遁走。

translations.literal: Fifth year, Xian crossed Luo challenged him, Yueyang fled away.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Xian crossed the Luo to challenge him; Yueyang fled.

sentences.zh: 是歲，明月又於汾北築城，西至龍門。

translations.literal: This year, Yueyang again at Fen north built city, west to Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yueyang again built a fort north of the Fen, west as far as Longmen.

sentences.zh: 晉公護問計於憲，憲曰：「兄宜暫出同州為威容，憲請以精兵居前，隨機攻取。」

translations.literal: Jin Duke Hu asked plan of Xian, Xian said: "Elder brother ought temporarily go out Tong province as awe appearance, Xian requests with picked troops go before, follow opportunity attack seize."
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jin, Hu, asked Xian's plan; Xian said, "Elder brother should temporarily go out to Tong province for a show of might; I request to lead picked troops forward and seize opportunities to attack."

sentences.zh: 六年，憲率眾出自龍門，齊將新蔡王康得潛軍宵遁。

translations.literal: Sixth year, Xian led masses out from Longmen, Qi general Xin'ai King Kangde secretly army night fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Xian led the army out from Longmen; the Qi Prince of Xin'ai, Kangde, secretly fled by night.

sentences.zh: 憲乃度河，攻其伏龍等四城，二日盡拔。

translations.literal: Xian then crossed river, attacked his Fulong and four cities, two days all taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then crossed the river and attacked his four walled cities Fulong and others — all were taken in two days.

sentences.zh: 又攻張壁，克之。

translations.literal: Again attacked Zhangbi, took it.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Zhangbi and took it.

sentences.zh: 斛律明月時在華容，弗能救，乃北攻姚襄城，陷之。

translations.literal: Hulu Yueyang then at Huarong, could not save, then north attacked Yaoxiang city, took it.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Yueyang was then at Huarong and could not save them; he went north and attacked Yaoxiang city and took it.

sentences.zh: 汾州又見圍日久，憲遣柱國宇文盛運粟饋之。

translations.literal: Fen province again saw siege long days, Xian sent pillar Yuwen Sheng transport grain feed it.
translations.idiomatic: Fen province had long been besieged; Xian sent the pillar Yuwen Sheng to transport grain to feed them.

sentences.zh: 憲自入兩乳穀，襲克齊伯杜城。

translations.literal: Xian himself entered Liangru Valley, stormed took Qi city Bodu.
translations.idiomatic: Xian himself entered the Liangru Valley and stormed and took the Qi city Bodu.

sentences.zh: 使柱國譚公會築石殿城以為汾州之援。

translations.literal: Sent pillar Tan Gonghui build Shidian city to serve as Fen province relief.
translations.idiomatic: He had the pillar Tan Gonghui build Shidian city as relief for Fen province.

sentences.zh: 齊平原王段孝先、蘭陵王高長恭引兵大至，大將軍韓歡為齊人所乘，遂退。

translations.literal: Qi Pingyuan King Duan Xiaoxian, Lanling King Gao Changgong led troops greatly arrived, great general Han Huan by Qi men overcome, then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi Princes Pingyuan, Duan Xiaoxian, and Lanling, Gao Changgong, led great armies; General Han Huan was overcome by the Qi men and retreated.

sentences.zh: 憲身自督戰，齊眾稍卻。

translations.literal: Xian body personally supervised battle, Qi masses gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xian personally directed the battle and the Qi masses gradually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，乃各收軍。

translations.literal: Met sunset, then each gathered army.
translations.idiomatic: As night fell each side withdrew their troops.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護誅，武帝召憲入，免冠拜謝。

translations.literal: When Jin Duke Hu executed, Wu Emperor summoned Xian in, removed cap bowed apology.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Jin, Hu, was executed, Emperor Wu summoned Xian, who removed his cap and bowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「汝親則同氣，休戚共之，事不相涉，何煩致謝？」

translations.literal: Emperor said: "You kin then same breath, joy sorrow shared, matters not mutually involved, why trouble offer thanks?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are kin by the same breath — we share joy and sorrow; the matter does not involve you — why trouble yourself with apologies?"

sentences.zh: 乃詔憲往護第，收兵符及諸簿籍等。

translations.literal: Then ordered Xian go to Hu residence, collect military tallies and all registers.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Xian to go to Hu's residence and collect military tallies and all registers.

sentences.zh: 尋以憲為大塚宰。

translations.literal: Soon made Xian Grand Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xian was made Grand Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 時帝既誅宰臣，親覽朝政，方欲齊之以刑，爰及親親，亦為刻薄。

translations.literal: At that time emperor already executed chief minister, personally viewed court government, just wished regularize by punishments, extending to kin, also was harsh.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having killed the chief minister, personally oversaw court affairs and wished to regularize all by punishments; even toward kin he was harsh.

sentences.zh: 憲既為護所任，自天和後，威勢漸隆。

translations.literal: Xian already by Hu employed, from after Tianhe, power prestige gradually rose.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, having been used by Hu, from after Tianhe his power and prestige gradually grew.

sentences.zh: 護欲有所陳，多令憲奏。

translations.literal: Hu wished have something present, often had Xian memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu wished to make a proposal he often had Xian present it.

sentences.zh: 其間或有可不，憲慮主相嫌隙，每曲而暢之。

translations.literal: Among these perhaps some not acceptable, Xian feared lord minister estrangement, each softened and made clear.
translations.idiomatic: When something was not acceptable Xian feared estrangement between lord and minister and always softened and made it clear.

sentences.zh: 帝亦悉其此心，故得無患。

translations.literal: Emperor also fully knew this heart, therefore had no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also fully knew this loyalty, so he had no trouble.

sentences.zh: 然猶以威名過重，終不能平，雖遷授塚宰，實奪其權也。

translations.literal: Yet still because prestige name too heavy, finally could not be at ease, though transferred appointed minister of war, in reality stripped his power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because his renown was too great he could not finally be at ease; though he was transferred to minister of war he was in reality stripped of power.

sentences.zh: 開府裴文舉，憲之侍讀，帝嘗禦內殿引見，謂曰：「昔魏末不綱，太祖匡輔元氏；

translations.literal: Opening office Pei Wenju, Xian's tutor, emperor once at inner hall summoned saw, said: "Formerly Wei end laws disordered, Grand Ancestor assisted upheld Yuan clan;
translations.idiomatic: Attending gentleman Pei Wenju, Xian's tutor, was once summoned to the inner hall; the emperor said to him, "In late Wei the laws were in disarray; the Grand Ancestor assisted and upheld the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 有周受命，晉公復執威權。

translations.literal: Zhou received mandate, Jin Duke again wielded awesome power.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou received the mandate, the Duke of Jin again wielded power.

sentences.zh: 積習生常，便謂法應須爾。

translations.literal: Accumulated custom became constant, then said law ought must be so.
translations.idiomatic: Habit piled upon habit until people thought it must be so by law.

sentences.zh: 豈有三十歲天子可為人所制乎？

translations.literal: How could there be thirty-year Son of Heaven able be by others controlled?
translations.idiomatic: How could a thirty-year-old Son of Heaven be controlled by others?

sentences.zh: 且近代以來，又有一弊，暫經隸屬，便即禮若君臣，此乃亂時權宜，非經國之術。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent times since, again one ill, briefly passed subordination, then at once rites like lord minister, this is chaotic times expedient, not governing state's art.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in recent times there has been another ill: after brief subordination people at once treat each other like lord and minister — that was a wartime expedient, not the art of governing a state.

sentences.zh: 爾雖陪侍齊公，不得即同臣主。

translations.literal: You though attend Qi duke, must not at once same as minister lord.
translations.idiomatic: Though you attend Prince Qi you must not at once become like minister to lord.

sentences.zh: 且太祖十兒，寧可悉為天子？

translations.literal: Moreover Grand Ancestor ten sons, how could all be Sons of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: And the Grand Ancestor's ten sons — could they all be Sons of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 卿宜規以正道，無令兄弟自致嫌疑。」

translations.literal: You ought guide with correct path, do not let brothers themselves bring suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: You should guide him with the correct path and not let brothers bring suspicion on themselves."

sentences.zh: 文舉再拜而出，歸以白憲。

translations.literal: Wenju twice bowed and went out, returned to tell Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju bowed twice and withdrew, returned, and told Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲指心撫幾曰：「吾心公寧不悉？

translations.literal: Xian pointed heart stroked armrest said: "My heart public how could he not know?
translations.idiomatic: Xian pointed to his heart and stroked the armrest, saying, "My heart is public — can he not know it?

sentences.zh: 但當盡忠竭節耳，知復何言！」

translations.literal: Only ought exhaust loyalty utmost devotion, what more to say!"
translations.idiomatic: I need only exhaust loyalty and utmost devotion — what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Jiande third year, advanced rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande his rank was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 甯友劉休征獻王箴一首，憲美之。

translations.literal: Ning friend Liu Xiuzheng presented king admonition one piece, Xian praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuzheng of Ning submitted an "Admonition to Kings," and Xian praised it.

sentences.zh: 休征後又以箴上之，帝方翦削諸弟，甚悅其文。

translations.literal: Xiuzheng later again with admonition presented to emperor, emperor just curtailing younger brothers, greatly pleased its text.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzheng later submitted the admonition to the emperor; the emperor was then curtailing his younger brothers and greatly liked the text.

sentences.zh: 憲嘗以兵書繁廣，自刊為要略五篇，至是表陳之。

translations.literal: Xian once because military books prolix broad, himself abridged into essentials five sections, to this memorial presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had found military books too prolix and himself abridged them into an Essentials in five sections; now he presented them in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而稱善。

translations.literal: Emperor viewed and praised good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read them and praised them.

sentences.zh: 其秋，帝于雲陽寢疾，衛王直于京師。

translations.literal: That autumn, emperor at Yunyang bed ill, Wei King Zhi at capital.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the emperor was ill at Yunyang; Prince Zhi of Wei was in the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝召憲謂曰：「汝為前軍，吾亦續發。」

translations.literal: Emperor summoned Xian said: "You be vanguard army, I also shall follow dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Xian and said, "You shall be the vanguard army — I too shall follow."

sentences.zh: 直尋敗走。

translations.literal: Zhi soon defeated fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was soon defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝至京師，憲與趙王招俱入拜謝。

translations.literal: Emperor reached capital, Xian with Zhao King Zhao together entered bowed thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached the capital, Xian and Prince Zhao of Zhao both entered to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「管、蔡為戮，周公作輔，人心不同，有如其面。

translations.literal: Emperor said: "Guan, Cai were executed, Duke of Zhou made regent, men's hearts differ, like their faces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Guan and Cai were executed, the Duke of Zhou served as regent — men's hearts differ as faces differ.

sentences.zh: 但愧兄弟親尋干戈，於我為不能耳。」

translations.literal: Only ashamed brothers kin sought arms, for me it is inability."
translations.idiomatic: I only regret that brothers should hunt each other with arms — I have fallen short in that."

sentences.zh: 初，直內忌憲，憲隱而容之，且以帝母弟，每加友敬。

translations.literal: At first, Zhi inwardly resented Xian, Xian concealed yet tolerated him, moreover because emperor uterine younger brother, each time added friendship respect.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhi inwardly resented Xian; Xian concealed this and tolerated him, and because he was the emperor's uterine younger brother always treated him with friendship and respect.

sentences.zh: 晉公護之誅也，直固請及憲。

translations.literal: When Jin Duke Hu was executed, Zhi obstinately asked to include Xian as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Jin, Hu, was executed, Zhi insistently asked that Xian be implicated too.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「齊公心跡，吾自悉之，不得更有所疑。」

translations.literal: Emperor said: "Qi Duke mind footprints, I myself fully know, must not again have some suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Prince Qi's mind and conduct I know full well myself — you must not harbor further suspicion."

sentences.zh: 及文宣皇后崩，直又密啟憲飲酒食肉與平昔不異。

translations.literal: When Wen Xuan Empress Dowager died, Zhi again secretly reported Xian drank wine ate meat with usual no difference.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Chinu died, Zhi again secretly reported that Xian drank wine and ate meat no differently than before.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾與齊王異生，俱非正嫡，特為吾意，今袒括是同。

translations.literal: Emperor said: "I with Qi King different birth, both not legitimate heir, especially for my intent, now bare arm wrap same.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Prince Qi and I were born to different mothers; neither of us was the legitimate heir — I favored him of my own accord; now we bare the arm alike for mourning.

sentences.zh: 汝當愧之，何論得失。

translations.literal: You ought ashamed, what discuss gain loss.
translations.idiomatic: You ought to feel ashamed — what talk of right and wrong?

sentences.zh: 汝親太后之子，但須自助。」

translations.literal: You kin Empress Dowager's son, only need self help."
translations.idiomatic: You are the empress dowager's son — you need only help yourself."

sentences.zh: 直乃止。

translations.literal: Zhi then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi then stopped.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝將東討，獨與內史王誼謀之，余人莫知。

translations.literal: Fourth year, emperor would east attack, alone with director of palace affairs Wang Yi plotted, others none knew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the emperor planned an eastern campaign and discussed it only with the director of palace affairs Wang Yi; no one else knew.

sentences.zh: 後以諸弟才略，無出憲右，遂告之。

translations.literal: Later because younger brothers' talent strategy, none exceeded Xian right, then told him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because among his younger brothers' talent and strategy none surpassed Xian, he told him.

sentences.zh: 憲即贊成其事。

translations.literal: Xian at once endorsed accomplished the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xian at once endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 及大軍將出，憲表上金寶等一十六件以助軍資。

translations.literal: When great army about to march out, Xian memorialized gold treasures and sixteen items to aid military funds.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army was about to march, Xian memorialized gold, treasures, and sixteen other items to aid military funds.

sentences.zh: 詔不納，以憲表示公卿曰：「人臣當如此，朕貴其心耳，寧資此物。」

translations.literal: Edict not accept, with Xian's memorial showed dukes ministers: "Subjects ought be like this, I value his heart, rather than fund these things."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not accept them and showed Xian's memorial to the ministers, saying, "A subject should act like this — I value his heart, not these goods."

sentences.zh: 乃詔寧為前軍，趣黎陽。

translations.literal: Then ordered Xian as vanguard army, hasten Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Xian as vanguard to hurry to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 帝親圍河陰，未克。

translations.literal: Emperor personally besieged Heyin, not taken.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally besieged Heyin but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 憲攻拔武濟，進圍洛口，拔其東西二城。

translations.literal: Xian stormed took Wuji, advanced besieged Luokou, took its east west two cities.
translations.idiomatic: Xian stormed and took Wuji, advanced to besiege Luokou, and captured its eastern and western cities.

sentences.zh: 以帝疾班師。

translations.literal: Because emperor ill withdrew army.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor fell ill the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是歲，初置上柱國，以憲為之。

translations.literal: This year, first set senior pillar, made Xian it.
translations.idiomatic: That year the senior pillar rank was first established and Xian was made one.

sentences.zh: 五年，大舉東討，憲復為前鋒，守雀鼠穀。

translations.literal: Fifth year, great campaign east attack, Xian again vanguard, guarded Sparrow-Mouse Valley.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year a great eastern campaign was launched; Xian again served as vanguard and guarded Sparrow-Mouse Valley.

sentences.zh: 帝親圍晉州，憲進克洪洞、永安二城，更圖進取。

translations.literal: Emperor personally besieged Jin province, Xian advanced took Hongdong, Yong'an two cities, again planned advance seize.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally besieged Jin province; Xian advanced and took Hongdong and Yong'an, then planned further advances.

sentences.zh: 齊主聞晉州見圍，自來援之。

translations.literal: Qi ruler heard Jin province saw siege, himself came rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi ruler heard Jin province was besieged he came in person to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 時陳王純頓千里徑，大將軍永是公椿屯雞棲原，大將軍宇文盛守汾水關，並受憲節度。

translations.literal: At that time Chen King Chun held at Thousand-Li Path, great general Yongshi Duke Chun at Chicken-Roost Plain, great general Yuwen Sheng guarded Fen River Pass, all received Xian's command.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chun of Chen held at Thousand-Li Path, the great general Duke Chun of Yongshi at Chicken-Roost Plain, and General Yuwen Sheng at Fen River Pass — all under Xian's command.

sentences.zh: 憲密謂椿曰：「捕者詭道，汝今為營，不須張幕，可伐柏為庵，示有處所。

translations.literal: Xian secretly told Chun: "Hunters use decoy paths — you now make camp, need not stretch awnings, can cut cypress for hut, show there is a place.
translations.idiomatic: Xian secretly told Chun, "Hunters use decoy paths — when you make camp now, do not pitch awnings; cut cypress for a hut to show there is a dwelling.

sentences.zh: 令兵去之後，賊猶致疑。」

translations.literal: Let troops after leave, enemy still will suspect."
translations.idiomatic: After the troops leave the enemy will still be suspicious."

sentences.zh: 時齊主分軍萬人向千里徑，又令其眾出汾水關，自率大兵與椿對。

translations.literal: At that time Qi ruler divided army ten thousand toward Thousand-Li Path, again ordered his masses out Fen Water Pass, himself led great army face Chun.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler then sent ten thousand men toward Thousand-Li Path, had his main force come out through Fen River Pass, and himself led a great army to face Chun.

sentences.zh: 宇文盛馳告急，憲自救之，齊人遽退。

translations.literal: Yuwen Sheng galloped reported urgent, Xian self rescued, Qi men quickly retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Sheng galloped to report the emergency; Xian went to rescue in person and the Qi troops quickly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 盛與柱國侯莫陳芮逐之，多有斬獲。

translations.literal: Sheng with pillar Hou Mo Chen Rui pursued, many kills captures.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng with the pillar Hou Mo Chen Rui pursued them and took many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 俄而椿告齊眾稍逼，憲又救之。

translations.literal: Soon Chun reported Qi masses slightly pressing, Xian again rescued.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chun reported the Qi forces were pressing; Xian rescued again.

sentences.zh: 會椿被敕追還，率兵夜反。

translations.literal: Met Chun by edict recalled, led troops night reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was then recalled by edict and led his troops back by night.

sentences.zh: 齊人果謂柏庵為帳幕，不疑軍退，翌日始悟。

translations.literal: Qi men indeed thought cypress hut was tent curtains, not suspect army retreated, next day then knew.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi men took the cypress hut for tent curtains and did not suspect the army had withdrawn; only the next day did they realize.

sentences.zh: 時帝已去晉州，留憲後拒。

translations.literal: At that time emperor already left Jin province, left Xian rear to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already left Jin province and left Xian to hold the rear.

sentences.zh: 憲阻水為陣。

translations.literal: Xian blocked water made formation.
translations.idiomatic: Xian blocked the water and formed his battle line.

sentences.zh: 齊領軍段暢至橋。

translations.literal: Qi commanding general Duan Chang reached bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi commanding general Duan Chang reached the bridge.

sentences.zh: 憲隔水問暢姓名，暢曰：「領軍段暢也，公復為誰？」

translations.literal: Xian across water asked Chang's name, Chang said: "Commanding general Duan Chang, you again who?"
translations.idiomatic: Xian called across the water and asked Chang's name; Chang said, "Commanding General Duan Chang — and who are you?"

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「我虞候大都督耳。」

translations.literal: Xian said: "I frontier patrol grand commander only."
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "I am only a frontier patrol grand commander."

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「觀公言語，不是凡人，何用隱名位。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "Viewing your speech, not ordinary person, why use hide name rank."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "From your speech you are no ordinary man — why hide your name and rank?"

sentences.zh: 憲乃曰：「我齊王也。」

translations.literal: Xian then said: "I am Qi Prince."
translations.idiomatic: Xian then said, "I am Prince of Qi."

sentences.zh: 偏指陳王純已下，並以告之。

translations.literal: Pointed to Chen King Chun and below, all with told him.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to Prince Chun of Chen and those below and told him of them all.

sentences.zh: 暢鞭馬去，憲即命旋軍。

translations.literal: Chang whipped horse left, Xian then ordered turn army.
translations.idiomatic: Chang whipped his horse away; Xian then ordered the army to turn back.

sentences.zh: 齊人遽追之，戈甲甚銳。

translations.literal: Qi men quickly pursued, weapons armor very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi troops quickly pursued, their weapons and armor very keen.

sentences.zh: 憲與開府宇文忻為殿拒之，斬其驍將賀蘭豹子、山褥環等，齊眾乃退。

translations.literal: Xian with opening office Yuwen Xin as rear guard resisted, cut their fierce generals Helan Baozi, Shanru Huan and others, Qi masses then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Xian with Attending Gentleman Yuwen Xin as rear guard held them off and cut down their fierce generals Helan Baozi, Shanru Huan, and others; the Qi masses then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝又命憲援晉州。

translations.literal: Emperor again ordered Xian relieve Jin province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered Xian to relieve Jin province.

sentences.zh: 齊主攻圍晉州，帝次於高顯，憲率所部先向晉州。

translations.literal: Qi lord attacked besieged Jin province, emperor halted at Gaoxian, Xian led his section first toward Jin province.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler attacked and besieged Jin province; the emperor halted at Gaoxian; Xian led his troops first toward Jin province.

sentences.zh: 明日諸軍總集，稍逼城下。

translations.literal: Next day all armies total gathered, slightly pressed below city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the armies gathered and gradually pressed below the city.

sentences.zh: 齊人大陣于營南，帝召憲馳往觀之。

translations.literal: Qi men great formation at camp south, emperor summoned Xian gallop go view.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi formed a great battle line south of the camp; the emperor summoned Xian to gallop out and observe.

sentences.zh: 憲反命曰：「請破之而後食。」

translations.literal: Xian returned order said: "Please break them then eat.
translations.idiomatic: Xian returned and reported, "Let me break them first, then we shall eat.

sentences.zh: 帝悅。

translations.literal: Emperor pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 既而諸軍俱進，應時大潰，齊主遁走。

translations.literal: Soon all armies together advanced, responded time great rout, Qi ruler fled.
translations.idiomatic: Then all the armies advanced together; at once there was a great rout and the Qi ruler fled.

sentences.zh: 齊人復據高壁及洛女，帝命憲攻洛女，破之。

translations.literal: Qi men again held high walls and Luonu, emperor ordered Xian attack Luonu, broke it.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi again held the high walls and Luonu; the emperor ordered Xian to attack Luonu and he broke it.

sentences.zh: 齊主已走鄴，留其安德王延宗據并州。

translations.literal: Qi ruler already fled Ye, left his Ande King Yan Zong hold Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler had already fled to Ye and left his Prince of Ande, Yan Zong, to hold Bing province.

sentences.zh: 帝進圍其城，憲攻其西面，克之。

translations.literal: Emperor advanced besieged the city, Xian attacked its west face, took it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor advanced to besiege the city; Xian attacked the western face and took it.

sentences.zh: 延宗遁走，追而獲之。

translations.literal: Yan Zong fled away, pursued and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zong fled; they pursued and captured him.

sentences.zh: 以功進封第二子安城公質為河間王，拜第三子賓為大將軍。

translations.literal: For merit advanced enfeoff second son Ancheng Duke Zhi as Hejian King, appointed third son Bin great general.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit his second son, Duke Zhi of Ancheng, was advanced to Prince of Hejian, and his third son Bin was made great general.

sentences.zh: 仍詔憲趣鄴，進克鄴城。

translations.literal: Still ordered Xian hasten Ye, advanced took Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: He still ordered Xian to hurry to Ye; he advanced and took Ye city.

sentences.zh: 憲善兵謀，長於撫禦，摧鋒陷陣，為士卒先。

translations.literal: Xian skilled military strategy, excelled comforting controlling, crushed vanguard broke formations, for soldiers ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was skilled in military strategy and excelled at comforting and controlling troops; he crushed the vanguard and broke formations, going before the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 齊人聞風，憚其勇略。

translations.literal: Qi men hearing wind, feared his courage strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi, hearing of him, feared his courage and strategy.

sentences.zh: 齊任城王湝、廣甯王孝珩等守信都，復詔憲討之。

translations.literal: Qi Rencheng King Huo, Guangning King Xiao Heng and others held Xindu, again ordered Xian attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi Prince of Rencheng, Huo, Prince of Guangning, Xiao Heng, and others held Xindu; the emperor again ordered Xian to attack them.

sentences.zh: 仍令齊主手書招湝，湝不納。

translations.literal: Still ordered Qi ruler hand letter summon Huo, Huo not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the Qi ruler write a letter in his own hand to summon Huo; Huo would not submit.

sentences.zh: 憲軍過趙州，湝令間諜二人覘，候騎執以白憲。

translations.literal: Xian's army passed Zhao province, Huo ordered two spies scout, patrol riders seized reported Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian's army passed Zhao province, Huo sent two spies to reconnoiter; patrol riders seized them and reported to Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲乃集齊舊將，偏將示之曰：「吾所爭者大，不在汝等。」

translations.literal: Xian then gathered Qi old generals, partial commanders showed them: "What we contend is great, not in you.
translations.idiomatic: Xian gathered the old Qi generals and subordinate commanders and showed them, saying, "What we contend for is great — it does not lie with you.

sentences.zh: 即放還，令充使，乃與湝書。

translations.literal: Immediately released returned, made them envoys, then with Huo letter.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately released and returned them, made them envoys, and then wrote to Huo.

sentences.zh: 憲至信都，湝陣于城南，登張耳塚望之。

translations.literal: Xian reached Xindu, Huo formation south of city, ascended Zhang Er mound viewed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian reached Xindu, Huo drew up his line south of the city and ascended Zhang Er's mound to view them.

sentences.zh: 俄而湝所署領軍尉相願偽出略陣，遂降，湝殺其妻子。

translations.literal: Soon Huo's appointed commanding general Wei Xiangyuan feigned go patrol formation, then surrendered, Huo killed his wife children.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huo's appointed commanding general Wei Xiangyuan feigned going out to patrol the formation and then surrendered; Huo killed his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 明日擒湝及孝珩等。

translations.literal: Next day captured Huo and Xiao Heng and others.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they captured Huo and Xiao Heng and the rest.

sentences.zh: 先是稽胡劉沒鐸自稱皇帝，又詔憲督趙王招等平之。

translations.literal: Earlier Jiehu Liu Meiduo styled himself emperor, again ordered Xian supervise Zhao King Zhao and others pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jiehu leader Liu Meiduo had styled himself emperor; the emperor again ordered Xian to supervise Prince Zhao of Zhao and others to pacify him.

sentences.zh: 憲自以威名日重，潛思摒退。

translations.literal: Xian himself because prestige name daily heavy, secretly thought remove withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Xian himself, because his renown grew daily, secretly thought to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 及帝欲親征北蕃，乃辭以疾。

translations.literal: When emperor wished personally campaign northern frontier, then declined claiming illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to campaign in person against the northern frontier, he declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋而帝崩，宣帝嗣位，以憲屬尊望重，深忌之。

translations.literal: Soon emperor died, Xuan Emperor succeeded, because Xian noble prestige heavy, deeply resented.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor died and Emperor Xuan succeeded; because Xian's noble prestige was great he deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 時尚未葬，諸王在內居服。

translations.literal: Time not yet buried, all princes within wore mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The burial had not yet taken place and the princes were within wearing mourning.

sentences.zh: 司衛長孫覽總兵輔政，恐諸王有異志，奏令開府于智察其動靜。

translations.literal: Director of guards Sun Bu Changluan total troops assist government, feared princes other intent, memorial ordered opening office Yu Zhi observe their movements.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Guards Sun Bu Changluan commanded troops to assist the government and, fearing the princes had other designs, memorialized that Attending Gentleman Yu Zhi should observe their movements.

sentences.zh: 及山陵還，帝又命智就宅候憲，因是告憲有謀。

translations.literal: When mountain tomb returned, emperor again ordered Zhi at residence watch Xian, thereby reported Xian had plot.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial tomb procession returned, the emperor again ordered Zhi to wait at Xian's residence; thereby he reported that Xian had a plot.

sentences.zh: 帝遣小塚宰宇文孝伯謂憲曰：「今欲以叔為太師，九叔為太傅，十一叔為太保，何如？」

translations.literal: Emperor sent junior minister Yuwen Xiaobo told Xian: "Now wish make uncle Grand Mentor, ninth uncle Grand Tutor, eleventh uncle Grand Guardian, how?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Junior Minister of War Yuwen Xiaobo to tell Xian, "I now wish to make you Grand Mentor, the ninth prince Grand Tutor, and the eleventh prince Grand Guardian — what say you?"

sentences.zh: 憲辭以才輕。

translations.literal: Xian declined saying talent light.
translations.idiomatic: Xian declined, saying his talent was slight.

sentences.zh: 孝伯返命，復來曰：「詔王晚共諸王俱入。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo returned order, came again: "Edict prince evening together all princes all enter.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo returned with his report and came again: "The edict orders the prince to enter this evening together with all the princes.

sentences.zh: 既至殿門，憲獨被引進。

translations.literal: Reached palace gate, Xian alone summoned in.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the palace gate, Xian alone was summoned in.

sentences.zh: 帝先伏壯士于別室，至即執之。

translations.literal: Emperor first hid strong men in separate room, arrived then seized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had first hidden strong men in a side room; when he arrived they seized him.

sentences.zh: 憲辭色不撓，固自陳說。

translations.literal: Xian expression color not bent, firmly self stated.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's expression did not change and he firmly stated his case.

sentences.zh: 帝使于智對憲。

translations.literal: Emperor had Zhi confront Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zhi confront Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲目光如炬，與智相質。

translations.literal: Xian eyes like torches, with Zhi face each other.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's eyes were like torches as he faced Zhi.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「以王今日事勢，何用多言！」

translations.literal: Someone said: "With prince today situation, what use much speech!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Given the prince's situation today, what use is much speech!"

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「我位重屬尊，一旦至此，死生有命，寧復圖存？

translations.literal: Xian said: "My rank heavy kin noble, once to here, life death have fate, how again plot survive?
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "My rank is heavy and my kinship exalted — to come to this in a moment: life and death have their fate; how could I again plot to survive?

sentences.zh: 但老母在堂，恐留慈恨耳。」

translations.literal: Only old mother in hall, fear leave kind regret."
translations.idiomatic: Only my old mother is in the hall — I fear leaving her a mother's grief."

sentences.zh: 因擲笏於地，乃縊之。

translations.literal: Then threw tablet to ground, then strangled.
translations.idiomatic: He then threw his tablet to the ground and was strangled.

sentences.zh: 時年三十五。

translations.literal: Years then thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 帝以于智為柱國，封齊國公。

translations.literal: Emperor made Zhi pillar, enfeoffed Qi state duke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Zhi a pillar and enfeoffed him as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 又殺上大將軍安邑公王興、上開府獨孤熊、開府豆盧紹等，皆以昵於憲也。

translations.literal: Also killed senior great general Anyi Duke Wang Xing, upper opening office Dugu Xiong, opening office Dou Lu Shao and others, all because intimate with Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Senior Great General Wang Xing, Duke of Anyi, Upper Attending Gentleman Dugu Xiong, Attending Gentleman Dou Lu Shao, and others — all because they were close to Xian.

sentences.zh: 帝既誅憲，無以為辭，故托興等與憲結謀，遂加戮焉。

translations.literal: Emperor having executed Xian, no pretext, therefore pretended Xing and others with Xian plotted, then added execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having executed Xian, had no other pretext and therefore pretended that Xing and others had plotted with Xian, and then put them to death as well.

sentences.zh: 時人知其冤酷，咸雲伴憲死也。

translations.literal: People of the time knew injustice cruel, all said accompanied Xian in death.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time knew it was unjust and cruel and all said they had died in Xian's company.

sentences.zh: 憲所生達步幹氏，蠕蠕人也。

translations.literal: Xian's birth mother Lady Dabu Gan, Rouran person.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's birth mother was Lady Dabu Gan, a Rouran.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，上冊為齊國太妃。

translations.literal: Jiande third year, elevated to Qi state Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande she was elevated to Grand Consort of Qi.

sentences.zh: 憲有至性，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xian had utmost nature, served mother filial piety renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had a deeply filial nature and was renowned for serving his mother.

sentences.zh: 太妃舊患，屢經發動，憲衣不解帶，扶持左右。

translations.literal: Grand Consort old illness repeatedly flared, Xian clothes not untied belt, supported left right.
translations.idiomatic: The grand consort had a chronic illness that often flared; Xian did not loosen his belt for days and supported her at her side.

sentences.zh: 憲或東西從役，每心驚，母必有疾，乃馳使參問，果如所慮。

translations.literal: Xian sometimes east west followed campaign, each heart startled, mother must have illness, then galloped envoy inquire visit, truly as worried.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was on campaign east or west his heart would suddenly be troubled; he was sure his mother must be ill and would gallop off messengers to inquire — and it was always as he feared.

sentences.zh: 六子，貴、質、賨、貢、乾禧、乾洽。

translations.literal: Six sons: Gui, Zhi, Bin, Gong, Qianxi, Qianjia.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Gui, Zhi, Bin, Gong, Qianxi, and Qianjia.

sentences.zh: 貴字乾福，少聰敏，尤便騎射。

translations.literal: Gui style Qianfu, young clever especially skilled riding shooting.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, style name Qianfu, was clever as a boy and especially skilled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 始讀孝經，便謂人曰：「讀此一經，足為立身之本。」

translations.literal: First read Classic of Filial Piety, then told people: "Read this one classic, enough establish self root."
translations.idiomatic: When he first read the Classic of Filial Piety he told people, "To read this one classic is enough to be the root of establishing oneself."

sentences.zh: 十歲，封安定郡公。

translations.literal: Age ten, enfeoffed Anding commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: At age ten he was enfeoffed as Duke of Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 文帝始封此郡，未嘗假人，至是封焉。

translations.literal: Wen Emperor first enfeoffed this commandery, never lent others, to this enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had first enfeoffed this commandery and had never granted it to another — now it was granted to him.

sentences.zh: 年十一，從憲獵於監州，一圍中，手射野馬及鹿一十有五。

translations.literal: Age eleven, followed Xian hunt at Jian province, one encirclement within, hand shot wild horses and deer fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: At age eleven he followed Xian hunting in Jian province; in one drive he shot fifteen wild horses and deer with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，拜齊國世子。

translations.literal: Jiande second year, appointed Qi state heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiande he was appointed heir of Qi.

sentences.zh: 後出為豳州刺史。

translations.literal: Later went out as Bin province governor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went out to serve as governor of Bin province.

sentences.zh: 貴雖出自深宮，而留心庶政。

translations.literal: Gui though came from deep palace, yet attentive to common government.
translations.idiomatic: Though Gui came from the inner palace, he paid attention to ordinary administration.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，過目輒記，嘗道逢二人，謂其左右曰：「此人是縣党，何因輒行？」

translations.literal: Nature clever keen, passed eyes then remembered, once on road met two men, told his left right: "This person is county party member, why suddenly travel?"
translations.idiomatic: He was clever and remembered whatever he saw; once on the road he met two men and said to his attendants, "This man is a county party member — why is he traveling here?"

sentences.zh: 左右不識，貴便說其姓名，莫不嗟伏。

translations.literal: Left right did not recognize, Gui then stated their names, none not sighed submitted.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants did not know them; Gui then gave their names, and all were amazed and submitted.

sentences.zh: 白獸烽經為商人所燒，烽帥受貨，不言其罪。

translations.literal: White Beast beacon once by merchants burned, beacon commander received goods, did not speak his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The White Beast beacon had once been burned by merchants; the beacon commander took a bribe and did not report the crime.

sentences.zh: 他日，此帥隨例來參，貴乃問云：「商人燒烽，何因私放？」

translations.literal: Another day, this commander followed custom came pay respects, Gui then asked: "Merchants burned beacon, why privately release?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day that commander came to pay his respects as usual; Gui then asked, "Merchants burned the beacon — why did you release them privately?"

sentences.zh: 烽帥愕然，遂即首伏。

translations.literal: Beacon commander startled, then at once bowed confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The beacon commander was startled and at once confessed.

sentences.zh: 其明察如此。

translations.literal: His keen insight like this.
translations.idiomatic: His keen insight was like this.

sentences.zh: 卒時年十七，武帝甚痛惜之。

translations.literal: Died years seventeen, Wu Emperor greatly pained regretted.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventeen; Emperor Wu deeply mourned him.

sentences.zh: 質字乾佑，以憲勳封河間郡王。

translations.literal: Zhi style Qianyou, because Xian merit enfeoffed Hejian commandery king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, style name Qianyou, was enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian commandery for Xian's merit.

sentences.zh: 賓字乾禮，中壩公。

translations.literal: Bin style Qianli, Middle Dam duke.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, style name Qianli, Duke of Middle Dam.

sentences.zh: 貢出後莒莊公，乾禧，安城公。

translations.literal: Gong came out after Ju Duke Zhuang, Qianxi, Ancheng duke.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was adopted heir to Duke Zhuang of Ju; Qianxi was Duke of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 乾洽，龍涸公。

translations.literal: Qianjia, Longhu duke.
translations.idiomatic: Qianjia was Duke of Longhu.

sentences.zh: 並與憲俱被誅。

translations.literal: All with Xian together were executed.
translations.idiomatic: They were all executed together with Xian.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝將遷周鼎，招密欲圖之，以匡社稷。

translations.literal: Sui Wen Emperor about to move Zhou tripod, Zhao secretly wished plot him, to rectify state altars.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was about to seize the Zhou mandate, Zhao secretly plotted against him to preserve the state.

sentences.zh: 乃要隋文帝至第，飲於寢室。

translations.literal: Then invited Sui Wen Emperor to residence, drank in bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Emperor Wen of Sui to his residence and entertained him in the bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 招子員、貫及妃弟魯封、所親人史胄皆先在左右，佩刀而立。

translations.literal: Zhao's sons Yuan, Guan and consort's younger brother Lu Feng, intimate man Shi Zhou all first at left right, wore swords standing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's sons Yuan and Guan, his consort's younger brother Lu Feng, and his confidant Shi Zhou were all beforehand at his side, wearing swords and standing.

sentences.zh: 又藏兵刃于帷席間，後院亦伏壯士。

translations.literal: Again hid weapons in curtain mats between, rear courtyard also hid strong men.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons were also hidden among the curtains and mats, and strong men lay in wait in the rear courtyard.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝從者多在合外，惟楊弘、元胄胄弟威及陶徹坐戶側。

translations.literal: Sui Wen Emperor's followers mostly outside hall, only Yang Hong, Yuan Zhou Zhou's younger brother Wei and Tao Che sat beside door.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Emperor Wen of Sui's followers were outside the hall; only Yang Hong, Yuan Zhou, Yuan Zhou's younger brother Wei, and Tao Che sat by the door.

sentences.zh: 招屢以佩刀割瓜啖隋文，隋文未之疑。

translations.literal: Zhao repeatedly with wearing sword cut melon feed Sui Wen, Sui Wen did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao repeatedly cut melon with his sword to serve Sui Wen, who did not suspect him.

sentences.zh: 元胄覺變，扣刀而入。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhou sensed change, knocked sword entered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhou sensed something amiss and entered with his hand on his sword.

sentences.zh: 招乃以大觴親飲胄酒，又命胄向廚取漿。

translations.literal: Zhao then with great goblet personally drank Zhou wine, again ordered Zhou toward kitchen fetch broth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then with a great goblet personally made Zhou drink wine and again ordered Zhou to the kitchen to fetch broth.

sentences.zh: 胄不為之動。

translations.literal: Zhou did not move for it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou did not stir.

sentences.zh: 滕王逌後至，隋文降階迎，胄因得耳語曰：「公宜速出。」

translations.literal: Teng King You later arrived, Sui Wen descended steps welcome, Zhou thereby could whisper: "Your Grace ought quickly leave."
translations.idiomatic: Prince You of Teng arrived later; Sui Wen went down the steps to welcome him, and Zhou was thus able to whisper, "Your Grace ought to leave quickly."

sentences.zh: 隋文共逌等就坐，須臾辭出。

translations.literal: Sui Wen with You and others took seat, soon excused left.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Wen sat with You and the others, then soon took his leave.

sentences.zh: 後事覺，陷以謀反，其年秋，誅招及其子德廣公員、永康王貫、越公乾銑、弟乾鏗等，國除。

translations.literal: Later matter discovered, framed with plotting rebellion, that year autumn, executed Zhao and his sons Duke Guang of De Yuan, King Guan of Yongkang, Yue duke Qianxi, younger brother Qianheng and others, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later the plot was discovered; he was framed for rebellion; that autumn Zhao was executed together with his sons Duke Yuan of Deguang, Prince Guan of Yongkang, Duke Qianxi of Yue, his younger brother Qianheng, and others, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 招所著文集十卷。

translations.literal: Zhao's composed collected works ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's collected works ran to ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 譙孝王儉，字侯幼突。

translations.literal: Qiao Xiao King Jian, style Houyoutu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao of Qiao, Jian, style name Houyoutu.

sentences.zh: 武成初，封譙國公。

translations.literal: Wucheng beginning, enfeoffed Qiao state duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進為王。

translations.literal: Jiande third year, advanced to king.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande he was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 從平鄴，拜大塚宰。

translations.literal: Followed pacify Ye, appointed Grand Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the pacification of Ye and was appointed Grand Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 薨，子乾惲嗣，為隋文帝所害，國除。

translations.literal: Died, son Qianyun succeeded, by Sui Wen Emperor harmed, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Qianyun succeeded but was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui and the fief abolished.

sentences.zh: 冀康公通，字屈率突。

translations.literal: Ji Kang Duke Tong, style Qushuatu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Kang of Ji, Tong, style name Qushuatu.

sentences.zh: 武成初，封冀國公。

translations.literal: Wucheng beginning, enfeoffed Ji state duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 薨，子絢嗣。

translations.literal: Died, son Xuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died and his son Xuan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進為王。

translations.literal: Jiande third year, advanced to king.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande he was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 大定中，亦為隋文帝所害。

translations.literal: Dading within, also by Sui Wen Emperor harmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading era he too was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui.

sentences.zh: 國除。

translations.literal: State abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 滕聞王逌，字爾固突。

translations.literal: Teng Wen King You, style Erqutu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen of Teng, You, style name Erqutu.

sentences.zh: 少好經史，解屬文。

translations.literal: Young liked classics histories, understood compose literature.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved the classics and histories and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 武成初，封滕國公。

translations.literal: Wucheng beginning, enfeoffed Teng state duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng he was enfeoffed as Duke of Teng.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Jiande third year, advanced rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande his rank was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: Xuanzheng first year, advanced rank senior pillar.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was advanced to senior pillar.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，詔以荊州新野郡邑萬戶為滕國，逌出就國。

translations.literal: Daxiang first year, edict took Jing province Xinye commandery ten thousand households as Teng state, You went out to state.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daxiang an edict made the ten thousand households of Xinye commandery in Jing province the state of Teng, and You went out to his fief.

sentences.zh: 三年，朝京師，為隋文帝所害，並其子，國除。

translations.literal: Third year, attended capital, by Sui Wen Emperor harmed, together his sons, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he came to the capital, was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui together with his sons, and the fief abolished.

sentences.zh: 逌所著文章頗行於世。

translations.literal: You's composed articles rather circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The articles You composed circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝一男：陸夫人生紀厲王康，字乾安。

translations.literal: Xiao Min Emperor one son: Lady Lu bore Ji Stern King Kang, style Qian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaomin had one son: Lady Lu bore Prince Kang of Ji, style name Qian'an.

sentences.zh: 保定初，封紀國公。

translations.literal: Baoding beginning, enfeoffed Ji state duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王，出為利州總管。

translations.literal: Jiande third year, advanced rank to king, went out as Li province commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande his rank was raised to prince and he went out as commissioner over Li province.

sentences.zh: 康驕侈無度，遂有異謀，司錄裴融諫，康殺之。

translations.literal: Kang arrogant extravagant without measure, then had other plot, director of records Pei Rong remonstrated, Kang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was arrogant and extravagant without limit and then harbored other designs; Director of Records Pei Rong remonstrated and Kang killed him.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔賜康死。

translations.literal: Fifth year, edict granted Kang death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict ordered Kang to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 子湜嗣，大定中，為隋文帝所害，國除。

translations.literal: Son Shi succeeded, Dading within, by Sui Wen Emperor harmed, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi succeeded; in the Dading era he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui and the fief abolished.

sentences.zh: 明帝三男：徐妃生畢剌王賢。

translations.literal: Ming Emperor three sons: Lady Xu bore Bi Thorn King Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had three sons: Lady Xu bore Prince Xian of Bi.

sentences.zh: 後宮生豐王貞、宋王實。

translations.literal: Rear palace bore Feng King Zhen, Song King Shi.
translations.idiomatic: The rear palace bore Prince Zhen of Feng and Prince Shi of Song.

sentences.zh: 實出後宋獻公震。

translations.literal: Shi came out after Song Duke Gong Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was the adopted heir of Duke Gong Zhen of Song.

sentences.zh: 畢剌王賢，字乾陽。

translations.literal: Bi Thorn King Xian, style Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Bi, style name Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，封畢公。

translations.literal: Baoding fourth year, enfeoffed Bi duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding he was enfeoffed as Duke of Bi.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Jiande third year, advanced rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande his rank was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 曆荊州總管、大司空。

translations.literal: Passed through Jing province commissioner, Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commissioner over Jing province and Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 大象初，進上柱國、雍州牧、太師。

translations.literal: Daxiang beginning, advanced senior pillar, Yong province governor, Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daxiang he was advanced to senior pillar, governor of Yong province, and Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 明年，宣帝崩。

translations.literal: Next year, Xuan Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Emperor Xuan died.

sentences.zh: 賢性強濟，有威略，慮隋文帝傾覆宗祐。

translations.literal: Xian nature strong resolute, had authority strategy, feared Sui Wen Emperor would overturn clan blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was forceful and resolute with authority and strategy and feared Emperor Wen of Sui would overturn the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 言泄，並其子被害，國除。

translations.literal: Words leaked, together his sons harmed, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His words leaked out; he and his sons were killed and the fief abolished.

sentences.zh: 豐王貞，字乾雅。

translations.literal: Feng King Zhen, style Qianya.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhen of Feng, style name Qianya.

sentences.zh: 初封豐國公，建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: First enfeoffed Feng state duke, Jiande third year, advanced rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Feng; in the third year of Jiande his rank was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 大象初，為大塚宰。

translations.literal: Daxiang beginning, made Grand Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daxiang he was made Grand Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 大定中，並其子為隋文帝所害，國除。

translations.literal: Dading within, together his sons by Sui Wen Emperor harmed, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading era he and his sons were killed by Emperor Wen of Sui and the fief abolished.

sentences.zh: 武帝七男：李皇后生宣帝、漢王贊。

translations.literal: Wu Emperor seven sons: Empress Li bore Xuan Emperor, Han King Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had seven sons: Empress Li bore Emperor Xuan and Prince Zan of Han.

sentences.zh: 庫汗姬生秦王贄、曹王允。

translations.literal: Kuhan Ji bore Qin King Zan, Cao King Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Kuhan bore Prince Zan of Qin and Prince Yun of Cao.

sentences.zh: 馮姬生道王充。

translations.literal: Lady Feng bore Dao King Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng bore Prince Chong of Dao.

sentences.zh: 薛世婦生蔡王兌。

translations.literal: Lady Xue bore Cai King Dui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xue bore Prince Dui of Cai.

sentences.zh: 鄭姬生荊王元。

translations.literal: Lady Zheng bore Jing King Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng bore Prince Yuan of Jing.

sentences.zh: 宣帝三子：硃皇后生靜皇帝。

translations.literal: Xuan Emperor three sons: Empress Zhu bore Quiet Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan had three sons: Empress Zhu bore Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 王姬生萊王衍。

translations.literal: Wang Ji bore Lai King Yan.
translations.idiomatic: A royal concubine bore Prince Yan of Lai.

sentences.zh: 皇甫姬生郢王術。

translations.literal: Lady Huangfu bore Ying King Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huangfu bore Prince Shu of Ying.

sentences.zh: 衍及術並大象二年封，並為隋文帝所害，國除。

translations.literal: Yan and Shu both Daxiang second year enfeoffed, both by Sui Wen Emperor harmed, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Shu were both enfeoffed in the second year of Daxiang and both were killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; their fiefs were abolished.

sentences.zh: 論曰：昔賢之議者，咸以周建五等，曆載八百；

translations.literal: Comment says: Formerly worthies who discussed, all thought Zhou established five ranks, passed years eight hundred;
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: In former times those who discussed the matter all held that Zhou established the five ranks and lasted eight hundred years;

sentences.zh: 秦立郡縣，二世而亡。

translations.literal: Qin established commanderies counties, second generation then perished.
translations.idiomatic: Qin established commanderies and counties and perished in the second generation.

sentences.zh: 雖得失之跡可尋，是非之理互起，而因循莫變，復古未聞。

translations.literal: Though traces of gain loss can be traced, principles of right wrong rise and fall mutually, yet following custom none changed, restoring antiquity not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Though the traces of success and failure can be traced and the principles of right and wrong contend with each other, people clung to custom without change and restoring antiquity was not heard of.

sentences.zh: 良由著論者溺於貴遠，司契者難於易業，詳求適變之道，並未窮於至當也。

translations.literal: Truly because those who wrote theories drowned in valuing the distant, those who held contracts found it hard to change enterprise, carefully seeking path of suiting change, all not exhausted to utmost fitness.
translations.idiomatic: This was truly because theorists were infatuated with what was remote in time and those who held power found it hard to change their practices; when they sought in detail the way to suit changing circumstances they did not reach what was ultimately fitting.

sentences.zh: 嘗試論之：夫皇王迭興，為國之道匪一；

translations.literal: Once tried discuss it: husband emperors kings in turn rise, way of governing state not one;
translations.idiomatic: Let us try to discuss it: emperors and kings rise in succession, and the way to govern a state is not one alone;

sentences.zh: 聖賢間出，立德之指殊塗。

translations.literal: Sages worthies in between emerge, establish virtue's aim different paths.
translations.idiomatic: sages and worthies appear in turn, and the aim of establishing virtue takes different paths.

sentences.zh: 斯豈故為相反哉，亦云為政而已矣。

translations.literal: This how intentionally opposite, also said governing only.
translations.idiomatic: This is not intentionally to be opposite — it is only that governing is governing.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 五等之制，行于商、周之前；

translations.literal: Five ranks system, practiced before Shang Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: The system of five ranks was practiced before the Shang and Zhou;

sentences.zh: 郡縣之設，始于秦、漢之後。

translations.literal: Commanderies counties setting, began after Qin Han.
translations.idiomatic: the setting of commanderies and counties began after the Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 論時則澆淳理隔，易地則用舍或殊。

translations.literal: Discuss time then shallow pure principle separate, change land then use discard perhaps different.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by time, shallow and pure ages are separated in principle; judged by place, what is used or discarded may differ.

sentences.zh: 譬猶幹戚日用，難以成垓下之業；

translations.literal: Like shield axe daily use, hard complete Gaixia enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: It is like using shields and axes in daily life — hard to accomplish the enterprise of Gaixia;

sentences.zh: 稷嗣所述，不可施成周之朝。

translations.literal: Jisi what he stated, cannot apply Cheng Zhou court.
translations.idiomatic: what Jisi stated cannot be applied in the court of accomplished Zhou.

sentences.zh: 是知因時制宜者，為政之上務也；

translations.literal: Therefore know suit time suit measure, governing's upper task;
translations.idiomatic: Thus to suit the time and circumstances is the highest task of government;

sentences.zh: 觀人立教才，經國之長策也。

translations.literal: Observe men establish teaching talent, governing state's long strategy.
translations.idiomatic: to observe men and establish teaching is the long-term strategy of governing a state.

sentences.zh: 且夫裂封疆，建侯伯，擇賢能，署牧守，循名雖曰異軫，責實抑亦同歸。

translations.literal: Moreover split fief borders, establish marquises earls, choose worthy able, appoint governors guards, follow name though said different tracks, charge substance also same return.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to divide the fief, establish marquises and earls, choose the worthy and able, and appoint governors and guards — the names differ but the charge in substance is the same.

sentences.zh: 盛則與之共安，衰則與之共患。

translations.literal: Flourishing then with them share peace, declining then with them share trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In prosperity one shares peace with them; in decline one shares trouble with them.

sentences.zh: 共安系乎善惡，非禮義無以敦風共患寄以存亡，非甲兵不能靖亂。

translations.literal: Share peace tied to good evil, without rites righteousness no means cultivate wind share trouble entrusted to survival perish, without armor weapons cannot pacify chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Sharing peace depends on good and evil — without rites and righteousness there is no means to cultivate custom; sharing trouble is entrusted to survival or perish — without arms there is no means to quell chaos.

sentences.zh: 是以齊、晉帥禮，鼎業傾而復振；

translations.literal: Therefore Qi Jin led rites, tripod enterprise tilted yet again revived;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Qi and Jin led with rites and the royal enterprise, though toppling, revived again;

sentences.zh: 溫、陶釋位，王綱弛而更張。

translations.literal: Wen Tao released rank, royal net slack yet again stretched.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Tao relinquished rank and the royal net, though slack, was stretched anew.

sentences.zh: 然則周之列國，非一姓也，晉之群臣，非一族也，豈齊、晉忠於列國，溫、陶賢於群臣哉？

translations.literal: Then Zhou's various states, not one surname, Jin's various ministers, not one clan, how Qi Jin loyal to various states, Wen Tao worthy among various ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's various states were not of one surname and Jin's ministers were not of one clan — were Qi and Jin loyal to the states and Wen and Tao worthier than the other ministers?

sentences.zh: 蓋位重者易以立功，權輕者難以盡節故也。

translations.literal: Cover position heavy easy establish merit, power light hard exhaust full loyalty hence.
translations.idiomatic: Those of heavy position easily establish merit; those of light authority hardly exhaust full loyalty — that is why.

sentences.zh: 由斯言之，建侯置守，乃古今之異術；

translations.literal: From this speak, establish marquises set guards, is ancient modern's different arts;
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that establishing marquises and setting guards are techniques different in ancient and modern times;

sentences.zh: 兵權爵位，蓋安危之所階乎。

translations.literal: Military power rank position, cover safety danger's what they step on.
translations.idiomatic: military power and rank and position are what safety and danger step upon.

sentences.zh: 周文之初定關右，日不暇給，既以人臣禮終，未遑蕃屏之事。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen's beginning fixed Guan west, days not spare supply, already with subject rites end, not leisure screen wall matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Wen at first secured the Guanxi region, his days allowed no rest; he ended as a subject in rites and had no leisure for enfeoffing the imperial kin as screens.

sentences.zh: 晉蕩輔政，爰樹其黨，宗室長幼，並握兵權，雖海內謝隆平之風而國家有磐石之固矣。

translations.literal: Jin Dang assisted government, then planted his faction, clan house senior junior, all grasped military power, though within seas declined peaceful abundant wind yet state had bedrock firmness.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jin, Dang, assisted in government and planted his faction; young and old of the imperial clan all held military power — though the realm no longer knew the breeze of peace and abundance, the state yet had the firmness of bedrock.

sentences.zh: 武皇克翦芒刺，思弘政術，懲專朝之為患，忘維城之遠圖，外崇寵任，內結猜阻。

translations.literal: Wu Emperor able cut thorns, thought expand government arts, warned monopolizing court's harm, forgot screen city distant plan, outside honored favor trust, inside knotted suspicion obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was able to cut down thorns and wished to broaden government; he took warning from the harm of monopolizing the court and forgot the distant plan of making the imperial kin a protective wall — outwardly he honored and trusted them, inwardly he bred suspicion and obstruction.

sentences.zh: 自是配天之基，潛有朽壤之墟矣。

translations.literal: From this matching heaven's foundation, secretly had rotten soil ruins.
translations.idiomatic: From this the foundation that matched Heaven secretly held ruins of crumbling earth.

sentences.zh: 宣皇嗣位，凶暴是崇，芟刈先其本枝，削黜偏於公族。

translations.literal: Xuan Emperor succeeded position, fierce violent what he honored, mowed cut first its root branches, cut remove partial toward public clan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne and honored fierceness and violence; he mowed down the root branches first and cut back the public clan on every side.

sentences.zh: 以齊王之奇姿傑出，足可牢籠於前載。

translations.literal: With Qi King's wondrous bearing outstanding, enough could firmly cage in former records.
translations.idiomatic: With the wondrous bearing and outstanding talent of the Prince of Qi, he could well have been firmly held up as a model in former ages.

sentences.zh: 處周公之地，居上將之重，肋冠俗，攻戰如神，敵國系以存亡，鼎命由其輕重。

translations.literal: Dwelt Duke of Zhou's place, occupied supreme general's weight, force topped crowd, attack battle like spirit, enemy state tied to survival perish, tripod mandate by his light heavy.
translations.idiomatic: He stood in the place of the Duke of Zhou and bore the weight of supreme commander; his force topped the age and his battles were like a god's — enemy states were bound to survival or ruin and the imperial mandate rose or fell with his weight.

sentences.zh: 屬道消之日，挾震主之威，斯人而嬰斯戮，君子是以知國祚之不永也。

translations.literal: Belonged to way declining's day, carried shaking lord's awe, this man yet met this punishment, gentleman thereby knew state's fortune not long.
translations.idiomatic: In the days when the Way was fading he wielded the awe of one who could shake his lord — that such a man should meet such a punishment showed gentlemen that the state's fortune would not endure.

sentences.zh: 其餘雖地惟叔父，親則同生，假文能輔主，武能威敵，莫不謝卿士于當年，從侯服于郡國，號為千乘，位侔匹夫。

translations.literal: The rest though territory only uncle father, kin then same birth, suppose civil able assist lord, martial able awe enemy, none not declined minister in that year, followed marquis service in commanderies states, called thousand chariots, rank matched common man.
translations.idiomatic: The rest, though in territory they were uncles and fathers and in kinship they were uterine brothers — suppose they could assist the ruler in civil matters and awe the enemy in martial ones — all alike declined from ministers in their day, followed marquis service in the commanderies and states, were called lords of a thousand chariots, yet their standing matched a common man.

sentences.zh: 是以權臣乘其機，謀士因其隙，遷龜鼎速於俯拾，殲王侯烈于燎原，悠悠邃古，未聞茲酷。

translations.literal: Therefore powerful ministers rode their opportunity, strategists used their gaps, moved turtle tripod swift as bending pick up, exterminated kings marquises fierce as prairie fire, far far deep antiquity, not heard this cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Thus powerful ministers seized their opportunity and strategists used their gaps; the sacred vessel was moved as swiftly as bending to pick something up and kings and marquises were exterminated as fiercely as a fire across the plain — in the long reaches of deep antiquity such cruelty was not heard of.

sentences.zh: 豈非摧枯振朽，易為力乎？

translations.literal: How not break withered shake rotten, easy as strength?
translations.idiomatic: Was it not like breaking withered wood and shaking rotten timber — easy to apply force?

sentences.zh: 向使宣皇擇姬、劉之制，覽聖哲之術，分命賢戚，布於內外，料其輕重，間以親疏，首尾相持，遠近為用，使其位足以扶危，其權不能為亂，事業既定，僥倖自息，雖使臥赤子，朝委裘，社稷固以久安，憶兆可以無患矣。

translations.literal: If had Xuan Emperor chosen Ji Liu's system, viewed sage wise arts, divided ordered worthy kin, spread inside outside, measured their light heavy, spaced by kin distant, head tail mutual hold, far near for use, made their position enough support danger, their power cannot make chaos, enterprise already settled, lucky schemes self cease, though made lie infant, court entrust fur robe, state altars solid thereby long peace, hundred million can without trouble.
translations.idiomatic: If Emperor Xuan had chosen the systems of the Ji and Liu houses and surveyed the arts of the sages, apportioned the worthy kin inside and outside, weighed their light and heavy duties and spaced them by kinship near and far, so head and tail held each other and far and near served their use — making their standing enough to support danger but their power unable to make chaos — once the enterprise was settled, scheming would have ceased of itself; though an infant lay abed and the court entrusted its affairs to a fur robe, the altars would have been secure in long peace and the millions could have been without trouble.

sentences.zh: 何後族之地而能窺其神器哉。

translations.literal: How later clan's ground able peep its sacred vessel?
translations.idiomatic: How could a later clan have peeped at the sacred vessel?

sentences.zh: 昔張耳、陳餘，賓客廝役，所居皆取卿相，而齊王之文武僚吏，其後亦多台牧，異代相符，可謂賢矣哉。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhang Er Chen Yu, guests servants, where dwelt all took minister chancellor, yet Qi King's civil martial officials clerks, their later also many terrace governors, different ages match, can said worthy!
translations.idiomatic: In former times Zhang Er and Chen Yu — guests and servants — wherever they dwelt produced ministers and chancellors; and the civil and martial officers of the Prince of Qi likewise later became many provincial governors — matching across different ages, they may be called worthy indeed!
